story.iWant: to log search patterns without collecting personal information
story.soThat: usage insights are available while maintaining privacy commitment
story.tasks:
- [ ] Task 1: Set up Upstash Redis client integration (AC: 1) - [ ] Install @upstash/redis SDK package - [ ] Create lib/redis.ts with Redis client configuration - [ ] Read UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN from environment variables - [ ] Export redis client instance for use in analytics module - [ ] Add TypeScript types for Redis configuration
- [ ] Task 2: Create analytics logging module with fire-and-forget pattern (AC: 1, 4, 5) - [ ] Create lib/analytics.ts module - [ ] Define AnalyticsEntry interface: { location: string, timestamp: string } - [ ] Implement logSearch(location: string) async function - [ ] Use redis.rpush() to append to 'analytics:searches' list - [ ] Implement fire-and-forget pattern: async execution, catch errors silently - [ ] Add console.error logging for analytics failures (never throw) - [ ] Return void (fire-and-forget, never blocks)
- [ ] Task 3: Integrate analytics into API route (AC: 1, 4, 5) - [ ] Import logSearch() into /app/api/check-rain/route.ts - [ ] Call logSearch(location) after successful forecast fetch - [ ] Use fire-and-forget pattern (don't await, let it run asynchronously) - [ ] Ensure analytics logging does not block response generation - [ ] Position call after input validation, before or after weather fetch (non-blocking)
- [ ] Task 4: Update environment variables documentation (AC: 1, 3) - [ ] Add UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL to .env.example - [ ] Add UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN to .env.example - [ ] Document Upstash Redis setup in .env.example comments - [ ] Note that these variables auto-populate when using Vercel Marketplace integration
- [ ] Task 5: Create TypeScript type definitions for analytics (AC: 1) - [ ] Create /types/analytics.ts file - [ ] Define AnalyticsEntry interface: { location: string, timestamp: string } - [ ] Define RedisConfig interface: { url: string, token: string } - [ ] Export all analytics-related types
- [ ] Task 6: Manual testing and validation (AC: 1-5) - [ ] Test API endpoint with valid location: verify analytics logged to Redis - [ ] Test API endpoint: verify response time not impacted (<2 seconds still met) - [ ] Test with invalid Redis credentials: verify forecast still succeeds - [ ] Test with Redis unavailable: verify logging fails silently, forecast succeeds - [ ] Verify logged data contains only location + timestamp (no PII) - [ ] Check Redis list 'analytics:searches' for logged entries - [ ] TypeScript compilation passes (`npm run type-check`) - [ ] ESLint validation passes (`npm run lint`)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. **Given** a location search is processed **When** analytics logging occurs **Then** only location (as entered) and timestamp are logged **And** no IP addresses, user agents, or session IDs are stored **And** logs are written to Upstash Redis (serverless database) **And** logging does not impact API response time **And** logging failures do not break the main request flow

constraints.constraint: Fire-and-forget pattern: Analytics logging must NEVER block the main request flow. Use async execution with silent error catching (try/catch with console.error only).
Privacy-first: ONLY log location (as entered) and timestamp (ISO 8601). NO IP addresses, user agents, session IDs, or any PII.
Error handling: Analytics functions must NEVER throw errors. Catch all errors, log to console.error, continue silently.
Performance: Analytics logging must not add >100ms to API response time. Target total response time remains <2 seconds.
TypeScript strict mode: No 'any' types. All interfaces explicitly defined in types/analytics.ts.
Environment variables: Use env constant from lib/env.ts for type-safe access to UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN.
Redis operations: Use rpush command for append-only logging to 'analytics:searches' list. Store JSON stringified entries.
Module separation: Create separate lib/redis.ts (client), lib/analytics.ts (logging logic), types/analytics.ts (types).
Testing: Manual testing only (no automated tests per Epic 2 standards). Verify fire-and-forget behavior by testing with Redis unavailable.

tests.standards: Per Epic 2 Technical Specification, automated unit tests are deferred to Epic 5. Manual testing approach is required: - TypeScript compilation validation (npm run type-check) - ESLint validation (npm run lint) - Manual endpoint testing with curl/Postman - Verify Redis logging via Upstash dashboard or Redis CLI - Test fire-and-forget pattern by breaking Redis credentials and verifying forecast still succeeds - Verify performance impact (<2 seconds response time maintained)
tests.locations: No automated test files for Epic 2. Manual testing via: - curl commands to POST /api/check-rain endpoint - Upstash Redis dashboard to verify logged entries - Console logs to verify silent error handling

test.approach: Call POST /api/check-rain with valid location. Check Upstash Redis dashboard for new entry in 'analytics:searches' list. Verify entry contains only location and timestamp fields.

test.description: Test fire-and-forget pattern with Redis unavailable
test.approach: Temporarily set invalid Redis credentials in .env.local. Call API endpoint. Verify forecast still succeeds with 200 OK response. Check server logs for console.error message about analytics failure.
Measure API response time before and after analytics integration. Verify response time still <2 seconds. Use curl with -w option to measure total time.
Check Redis entries via Upstash dashboard. Verify ONLY location and timestamp fields present. Confirm no IP address, user agent, session ID, or other PII.
Run npm run type-check (verify zero errors). Run npm run lint (verify zero errors). Ensure strict mode compliance with no 'any' types.
